newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Job of NAR wins Tobago by-election.
newsitem.headline: Job of NAR wins Tobago by-election.

text.p: Morgan Job, a 56-year-old agricultural economist, won Monday's by-election in Tobago, election officials announced early on Tuesday.
The Tobago East seat was made vacant following the elevation of Ray Robinson, the then member of Parliament, to the post of president of Trinidad and Tobago in February.

According to preliminary results, Job, candidate of the National Alliance for Reconstruction (NAR), received 4,117 votes, while his two opponents - Hilson Phillips of the People's National Movement (PNM) got 1,184, with independent Winford James fetching 816 votes.
There were 16,823 voters on the registered list.
Under the constitution, the 116 square mile (300 sq km) island is allowed two MPs in the national parliament.
The Tobago West district is represented by Pamela Nicholson, Minister of Sports and Youth Affairs.
The NAR is the minority partner in the 17-year-old coalition government headed by Prime Minister Basdeo Panday, a British-trained lawyer of East Indian stock.
Panday's party -- the United National Congress (UNC) -- is the majority partner in the coalition administration that came to power following inconclusive general elections on Nov. 6, 1995.
